description:
SpacePulse is a health monitoring web app for astronauts on long space missions. We have an early prototype and will develop it further during the hackathon using NASA challenge data.

Looking for teammates in:
- Graphic design and slides
- Writing and pitch
- Demo video
- Data analysis and visualization
- Health or biology knowledge

No coding needed. If you are reliable, send a request to join.
summary:
AstroVitals is an offline-first health monitoring web app that helps astronauts on long space missions spot health changes early and act on them. It answers the challenge by gathering health indicators and helping crew members evaluate their own status.

Crew members log vitals, radiation dose, bone density loss, cabin conditions (CO2, humidity, temperature, pressure) and a short cognitive test. A risk engine combines them into one 0-100 score with green, yellow or red status, forecasts risk for the next 7 days, and suggests countermeasures based on NASA Human Research Program (HRP) research.

A live Hazard Coverage panel maps the results to NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight: radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile closed environments. A flight surgeon dashboard gives doctors a whole-crew view, and offline support keeps the app working when communication is delayed.

Far from Earth, astronauts cannot count on quick medical help, so early warning and self-monitoring matter for future Moon and Mars missions. Demo vitals are simulated; no real astronaut data is used.
details: What it does AstroVitals lets astronauts log daily vitals such as SpO2, sleep and stress, radiation dose, bone density loss, cabin conditions (CO2, humidity, temperature, pressure) and a short cognitive test (reaction time, memory, isolation score). It also tracks medications and allergies. How it works A Flask and SQLite backend feeds a risk engine that combines these inputs into one 0-100 score with green, yellow or red status. A 7-day forecast extends recent trends. Countermeasure suggestions for bone loss, radiation, sleep and stress are based on NASA Human Research Program (HRP) research. A Hazard Coverage panel maps flagged factors to NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight. A flight surgeon dashboard summarizes the whole crew, a printable report is available, and a PWA service worker keeps the app usable offline. Benefits and intended impact Astronauts on long missions carry much of the responsibility for spotting health changes in themselves. AstroVitals gives them early warnings and clear next actions, and gives doctors on Earth a quick overview when communication is delayed. It is a foundation for crew health autonomy tools for future Moon and Mars missions. Tools used Python, Flask, SQLite, NumPy, Chart.js, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Progressive Web App, hosted on PythonAnywhere. Creativity and factors considered Instead of showing isolated numbers, the app ties every metric to NASA's five hazards, so a crew member can see which hazard is rising. I considered offline use, simple language for non-specialists, and honesty about the limits of the data. Data and development notes All vitals in the demo are simulated; no real astronaut data is used. Risk thresholds are app-defined and not clinically validated. The working version submitted here was built during the hackathon. Super Intelligence (SI) use Claude (by Anthropic) was used for help with coding and debugging, writing and editing this text, researching NASA hazard information, and creating the demo slides. The app does not call any AI service at runtime. Final decisions, testing and deployment were done by me.
